guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.overvi: A machine combines a $(l:mmcr:controllers/controller)controller$(/l), structure, and components.$(br2)Controllers check structure and manage operation. Ports handle materials, energy, and products. Casings provide structure. Choose parts to match the machine.

Machines come from modpacks or addons. Without machine content, there may be no controllers; this guide remains readable.$(br2)Parallelism, factories, upgrades, and modules need machine support. Nearby placement alone does not make a component recognized.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.acquis: Craft an ordinary book with a Modularium Ingot to obtain the Modular Guide. Ingredient positions do not matter.
Modularium Ingots are crafting materials for many components. An ingot is not a machine controller and provides no operating capability by itself. Consult your recipe viewer for component recipes.

With Patchouli, find the guide in the MMCR creative tab. Hold it in your main hand and right-click to open.$(br2)Its enchanted-book appearance is temporary, not an enchanting ingredient. Without Patchouli, neither the guide nor its recipe is provided.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.casing: Basic casings provide structure; they neither process recipes nor store inputs or outputs. Follow the machine preview. Only replace casings with ports where permitted. See $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)structure checks$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.c: The controller is the machine's entry point. Each is registered with machine content; none substitutes for every machine.$(br2)Without machine content, no controllers is normal. This chapter remains readable without one.

Facing orients the structure. Vertical placement needs machine support; facing depends on the clicked face and player position.$(br2)Place the controller first, then check with a $(l:mmcr:tools/blueprint)blueprint$(/l) or $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l). Horizontal-only machines cannot face vertically.

$(l:mmcr:processing/factory)Factory controllers$(/l) schedule supported machines; they do not replace machine controllers.$(br2)The machine's own controller still checks structure and runs recipes. It shows factory threads when enabled. The factory component's screen holds thread-capacity items.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.f: Right-click normally for the screen.$(br2)For an unformed machine, empty both hands and sneak-right-click to preview and check immediately. Formed controllers do not use this preview action. A $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l) can also request checks.

Check block types, states, positions, and counts. Port direction, family, and tier may matter; larger ports are not always valid substitutes.$(br2)Choose the correct structure stage and satisfy machine-level slot requirements too.

Sharing follows machine rules; overlapping structures cannot automatically share every port.$(br2)Keep the area loaded. Fix the first reported mismatch or failed requirement, then recheck. Once formed, inspect $(l:mmcr:controllers/operation)operating conditions$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.o: Formed does not mean running.$(br2)Read status, recipe, and progress. Idle, no recipe, insufficient resources, and paused are different states. During operation, product and energy information reflects the current recipe and actual parallelism.

Check the selected recipe pool, if selectable.$(br2)Machine level comes from conditions such as level slots; structure stage is a whole structure phase. Recipes can require both, even with correct materials. Only the machine's available pools supply recipes.

Direct redstone signals pause the controller. Removing them does not waive structure or resource conditions.$(br2)Follow the failure reason: inputs, energy, output space, or extra conditions. Appearance alone is insufficient. See $(l:mmcr:troubleshooting/common)troubleshooting$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.items.p: Input buses hold items for recipes to consume. Right-click to insert materials, or supply them from external storage. The machine must recognize the bus as a valid input component.
Output buses receive machine products and need compatible free space. They are not input buses: placing raw materials on the output side does not make the machine consume them there.

Normal bus tiers differ in slot layout. $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_items)Extended item buses$(/l) store bulk items and display actual amounts. Larger storage does not relax structure rules.$(br2)For automatic supply or product removal, choose resource type and faces on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO page$(/l).
Fluid input hatches supply recipe fluids. Normally right-click with a supported fluid container to interact according to port direction and container capabilities, or connect fluid transport equipment.
Fluid output hatches receive fluid products for removal by containers or transport equipment. Incompatible contents or insufficient free space can block output.

For bulk storage, see $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_fluids)extended fluid hatches$(/l). Check fluid type, amount, capacity, and $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO faces$(/l).$(br2)Missing input and blocked output are separate problems. Chemicals are not ordinary fluids and cannot be stored here.
Energy input hatches store energy consumed by machines. Connect a working supply and check the required input tier. Insufficient stored energy can interrupt recipe operation.
Energy output hatches receive energy from generating recipes and transfer it to external consumers. They do not replace input hatches; a power-consuming machine still needs a recognized input.

Capacity is stored amount; rate is delivery speed. $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_energy)Extended energy hatches$(/l) offer larger buffers, but cables and sources may limit supply.$(br2)For unstable operation, check stored energy, supply, and $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l), not capacity alone.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.combine: A combined input port provides item and fluid inputs in one block. Each resource has separate storage and auto-IO settings. Use it where the structure permits combined input.
A combined output port receives both item and fluid products. Both need compatible space; blockage on either side can affect the recipe. It does not provide energy input.

$(l:mmcr:ports/extended_combined)Extended combined ports$(/l) provide bulk storage for both resources. Structure and port rules decide whether they replace separate buses or hatches.$(br2)Configure items and fluids separately on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO page$(/l). One switch does not enable every resource.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.auto_io: Open a supported port and switch to auto IO. Select each resource separately on multi-resource ports.$(br2)Inputs pull from neighbors; outputs push to them. Master and side switches apply to the selected resource type.

Toggle the six faces; buttons can show neighbors. These permissions change transfer faces, not the input/output role.$(br2)The master switch must be on too. Neighbors must support the resource and allow extraction or insertion.

Input ports can Eject Contents to neighbors, not world drops. Click for the first resource kind; Shift-click for all kinds.$(br2)Active-recipe ports cannot eject. Without a receiver, contents stay inside. Output ports do not use this button.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.pa: Parallel controllers raise the batch-processing limit for a supported machine. Tiers have different limits; the effective result still depends on machine and recipe settings.

Parallelism batches copies of one recipe; it does not add independent threads.$(br2)Actual batches depend on materials, output space, energy, and machine conditions, not just the limit. Check $(l:mmcr:ports/items)items$(/l), $(l:mmcr:ports/fluids)fluids$(/l), and $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.fa: Factory controllers schedule multiple recipe threads for factory-capable machines. Put this component in a permitted structure position. It is not a complete machine on its own.

The factory screen shows thread status and progress. Threads run independently; $(l:mmcr:processing/parallel)parallelism$(/l) batches work within one.$(br2)$(l:mmcr:processing/thread_disperser)Thread Rippers$(/l) add capacity. Machine limits, recipe thread caps, and shared input/output resources still apply.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.th: Right-click the factory controller component and place Thread Rippers in its dedicated item slot. That slot accepts only Thread Rippers. Do not put them in a normal input bus or upgrade bus for this purpose.

Slot contents contribute to thread capacity; changes update the linked factory.$(br2)This is not a CPU setting or a guarantee of one running recipe per item. Check $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory support$(/l), resources, and recipe thread limits first.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.up: Upgrade buses hold upgrade items supported by the machine. Bus families offer different slot counts. Being able to insert an item does not mean the machine defines an upgrade effect for it.

Use a recognized bus and specified upgrades. Effects, supported types, and stacking rules depend on the machine and upgrades.$(br2)No effect? Check recognition and item support. Ordinary materials and thread-capacity items are not universal upgrades.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.sm: Smart interfaces provide editable numeric parameters for a linked machine. Available types come from that machine. Without a valid binding or defined parameters, there is nothing to edit.

Use Previous/Next to read each parameter's description and value. Enter a number, then Save or press Enter. Integers reject fractions.$(br2)Parameters affect machine-defined conditions or effects. A saved value may still fail a recipe condition.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.da: Data storage holds a linked machine's runtime data. It is not an item chest and provides no ordinary item input/output. Use it when required by the machine's structure and behavior.

Data storage links to at most one controller. The machine saves and reads its data; display and effects are machine-specific.$(br2)No displayed data need not be a fault. Check that the machine needs this component and recognizes its position.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.mo: A module bridge connects a supported host and module. Both structures must use the same bridge at valid positions, and the host must allow that module type.

Form both structures, then check host connection. An offline module may not run.$(br2)The bridge needs one valid host/module pair. Overlapping functional interfaces can conflict. Check allowed types, structures, and bridge positions; proximity alone is insufficient.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.bluepri: Sneak-right-click a machine controller with a blueprint to bind its machine. Then hold the blueprint in your main hand and right-click the air normally to open the preview. An unbound blueprint shows a message.

Plus/minus select layers; A shows all; R resets. Multi-stage machines also have stage buttons.$(br2)Layers are viewing slices; stages are whole structure phases. Click preview blocks for replacement candidates. Materials reflect the current preview.

Shift expands tooltip materials for the lowest stage and default level blocks, not every higher-level combination.$(br2)Check the screen's stage and replacements. Select building levels with a $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l). Blueprints do not place blocks automatically.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.termina: Main-hand sneak-right-click binds a controller. Air right-click opens the screen; sneak-use in air unbinds the controller and resets structure selections and preview. Stay within operating distance.

Inventory uses your materials. Select container mode, then sneak-right-click a valid container to bind.$(br2)Clear keeps storage mode and bindings. Choose stage and levels; inspect preview, layers, and $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)Check$(/l). Checking is not building.

Build uses selected storage and permitted blocks. Resolve reported shortages or existing mismatches.$(br2)Demolish targets the selected structure and returns recoverable items to selected storage. Leave room for returns; it is not a region-mining tool.

Keep the terminal in your main hand. The controller must be loaded, in the same dimension, and within the configured radius.$(br2)Unavailable storage prevents build/demolish. Preview proves no requirements. Follow binding, distance, and material messages.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.export_: The multiblock detector marks structures for creation and export. Right-click a block for the first corner; sneak-right-click for the second. While holding the tool, use Pick Block to mark the controller position and face.

Main-hand air right-click opens settings; sneak-use in air clears selection. The tooltip lists recorded positions.$(br2)Ordinary survival building needs no export tool. Inspect with a $(l:mmcr:tools/blueprint)blueprint$(/l) and build with a $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.network.inter: A network interface is a machine-network endpoint that must be recognized by a valid formed machine. It is not an AE2 ME interface, and connecting a cable does not make it an ME storage port.

Connections need machine support, allowed endpoint types, free connection capacity, and valid machine states.$(br2)Use a $(l:mmcr:network/key_card)key card$(/l) to select source and target. Adding an interface does not give every machine new network features.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.network.key_c: Sneak-right-click a valid network interface to select the source endpoint. Normally right-click the target interface to attempt a connection. Sneak-use in the air to clear the card's selection.

Select a source belonging to a valid formed machine. Invalid endpoints, disallowed types, or full capacity reject connections with a message.$(br2)The card is not a universal remote. Check $(l:mmcr:network/interfaces)endpoint conditions$(/l), then reselect if needed.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.troubleshooti: $(bold)Structure first$(reset)$(br)Check facing, blocks, port tiers, stage, and loaded chunks with $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)formation checks$(/l).$(br2)Then verify the recipe pool, machine level, and structure stage support the target recipe.

$(bold)Resources next$(reset)$(br)Use $(l:mmcr:ports/items)inputs$(/l), enough $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy$(/l), and compatible output space.$(br2)Check $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l): resource, master switch, faces, and neighbors. Higher parallelism needs more materials and output space.

$(bold)Extra conditions$(reset)$(br)Remove pausing redstone signals. Check $(l:mmcr:components/modules)module connections$(/l) and $(l:mmcr:components/smart_interface)parameters$(/l).$(br2)Capacity is not active threads; an offline network is not a missing structure. Follow the controller's status and failure reason.
Connect to an ME network and configure items or fluids to stock in the interface screen. Normal input interfaces first stock their own storage; the machine consumes this local inventory.

Meet machine structure rules and ME network conditions. Check actual interface contents, not just stocking targets.$(br2)A configured target is not owned material. For direct network-stock consumption, see $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_stocking_input)stocking inputs$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_stocki: Configure the item or fluid types the machine may use. Stocking inputs consume ME network inventory directly. Displayed storage amounts mirror network stock, not a separate local cache already collected in the block.

Unlike $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_input)normal inputs$(/l), no local stock accumulates. Recipes extract configured types from ME; settings do not create inventory.$(br2)Keep the network usable and stocked. Disconnection or other consumers change displayed and available amounts.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_output: Send machine items and fluids into the ME network. Normal output interfaces have a bounded local cache; network scheduling continues moving cached products into storage.

Offline ME or insufficient compatible space stops draining. A full cache then blocks machine output.$(br2)Check power, connectivity, and storage. This is output, not input stocking. $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_async_output)Async outputs$(/l) buffer differently.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_async_: Async outputs receive products in a temporary in-memory queue, then send batches through ME network scheduling. They do not use the normal output's persisted local cache and have no offline-storage fallback.

Unloading, removal, or inactive nodes clear undelivered contents. Keep network and chunks available.$(br2)Async means neither unlimited capacity nor guaranteed speed. Acceptance needs network insertion space. For local caching, use $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_output)normal outputs$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_patter: Insert processing patterns matching machine recipes and connect the interface to ME. It coordinates AE2 crafting requests with linked machines; it cannot make a machine execute a recipe it does not have.

Starts require formed, runnable machines, matching recipes, resources, idle threads, and batch/thread limits.$(br2)Products enter the provider's return inventory. AE2 returns them to ME to settle crafting. If ME cannot accept them, resolve return blockage.

Pattern and blocking settings govern request continuation, not exemptions from structure, redstone, or resource rules.$(br2)Distinguish $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory threads$(/l) from $(l:mmcr:processing/parallel)batch parallelism$(/l). For stalls, inspect machine status and AE2 return inventory.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.terminal_: Choose ME inventory mode in the terminal, then hold it in your main hand and sneak-right-click a valid AE2 wireless access point. Bind the machine controller separately. An ordinary container is not a wireless access point.

Use a loaded, active access point with network inventory. Build extracts materials; demolition returns items.$(br2)Controller dimension and distance limits still apply. Follow shortages, network failures, and return failures. See $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal basics$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.extendedae.in: Extended inputs offer more configuration and storage slots, still stocking locally before machine consumption. Direction matches $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_input)normal inputs$(/l); network and structure requirements still apply.

Extended stocking inputs configure more resource types while retaining $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_stocking_input)direct network consumption$(/l). More slots do not turn the displayed network-stock mirror into a local cache.
Extended outputs offer a larger slot layout with bounded local caching. $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_output)Normal output blockage conditions$(/l) still apply; expanded capacity is not unlimited network space.

Oversize inputs use an oversize interface storage layout and still stock locally. Check configuration and amounts in the screen. Whether the port can replace another structure block remains the machine's decision.
Oversize outputs use the oversize storage layout to send machine products into ME. Insufficient network space still blocks output. They are not async output interfaces.

Extended pattern interfaces provide more pattern slots while retaining $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_pattern)pattern requests and product returns$(/l). More pattern slots do not increase actual machine threads or remove resource limits.

Oversize stocking input is disabled in this version, not an obtainable component here. Use extended stocking input instead.$(br2)Input, stocking, output, and pattern interfaces have different roles. Larger-sounding names do not make them interchangeable.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.appflux.flux_: ME energy inputs supply machines from AppliedFlux's ME energy storage. They need a working network, extractable energy, and machine support for this input component. They provide no item or fluid input.

ME energy outputs send generated energy into AppliedFlux network storage. Insufficient acceptance space affects output. Input and output are not interchangeable; see $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy direction and supply$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.chem: Chemical inputs supply Mekanism recipes. Chemicals differ from ordinary fluids; fluid hatches are not substitutes. Normal chemical hatches accept only non-radioactive chemicals.
Chemical output hatches receive non-radioactive products for removal by chemical transport equipment. Check type, direction, and free space. A fluid pipe does not necessarily transport chemicals.

Hatch tiers differ in storage and may satisfy port-tier requirements. Larger capacity does not guarantee structure acceptance.$(br2)Check chemical type, amount, and $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l). Radioactive materials need $(l:mmcr:mekanism/radioactivity)radioactive hatches$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.radi: Radioactive inputs accept only chemicals with the radioactive property, for machine consumption. Normal chemical hatches reject these resources; radioactive hatches also reject ordinary non-radioactive chemicals.

Radioactive outputs receive radioactive chemical products. Extract them with a receiver supporting the resource, and confirm machine support for this port. It does not convert products into non-radioactive chemicals.

These ports do not purify, remove radiation, or process waste.$(br2)Removal invokes radiation dumping for contents when Mekanism radiation is enabled. Handle contents through valid transport before dismantling. Storage support does not mean radiation-free removal.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.heat: Heat inputs accept incoming external heat to satisfy machine heat or minimum-temperature conditions. Reaching a temperature threshold is not the same as storing enough heat. Check the actual recipe condition.

Heat outputs receive generated heat and transfer it to supported adjacent equipment. Output ports do not accept external heat coming in. Effective heat removal also depends on temperature difference and neighboring equipment.

Heat is energy; temperature is thermal state; heat capacity relates their changes. They are not interchangeable.$(br2)Cooler surroundings drain heat. Check readings, exposed faces, and recipe conditions. Heat ports are not ordinary energy hatches.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.extende: Extended Item Buses
Basic Input
The Basic extended input bus has 8 bulk storage positions for recipe materials. Each position holds an item type with its components. Use it for large reserves of the same materials.
Basic Output
The Basic extended output bus has 8 bulk storage positions for products. Right-click to check the stored types and actual amounts. It receives output; it does not supply recipe inputs.
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended input bus has 16 bulk storage positions. Choose it when a recipe pool needs more different materials than the Basic tier can hold. The structure must permit this input bus.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended output bus has 16 bulk storage positions. It buffers a wider range of products. Leave compatible positions available and configure automatic removal to keep production moving.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended input bus has 24 bulk storage positions. It suits machines with many ingredient types. A larger bus does not supply missing items or bypass recipe component requirements.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended output bus has 24 bulk storage positions. Use it to separate more product types. If every position holds an incompatible resource, a new product still has nowhere to go.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended input bus has 32 bulk storage positions, the largest layout in this family. Check ingredient quantities and components in its interface before starting the machine.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended output bus has 32 bulk storage positions. It is suited to large product buffers. External receivers still need compatible free space to accept automatic transfers.

All four tiers use large-quantity storage per position; upgrading increases the number of positions. Read actual amounts in the interface rather than treating them as ordinary stack sizes.$(br2)Use $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l) for supply or removal. Structure rules decide whether an extended bus can replace a normal one.
Extended Fluid Hatches
Basic Input
The Basic extended fluid input hatch has 8 bulk fluid storage positions. Supply the fluids required by the recipe through supported containers or neighboring fluid transport equipment.
Basic Output
The Basic extended fluid output hatch has 8 bulk fluid storage positions for products. Check each stored fluid and arrange compatible containers or transport equipment to remove it.
Advanced Input

The Advanced extended fluid input hatch has 16 bulk storage positions. It holds a wider selection of recipe fluids. Check fluid identity and quantity separately; more positions cannot replace a missing ingredient.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended fluid output hatch has 16 bulk storage positions. Reserve compatible positions for different products and configure removal for each fluid your machine produces.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended fluid input hatch has 24 bulk storage positions. It suits machines that use many fluid types. Stored chemicals are not ordinary fluids and require their own chemical ports.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended fluid output hatch has 24 bulk storage positions. A large buffer can still be blocked if no position accepts the next product or the connected receiver cannot take it.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended fluid input hatch has 32 bulk storage positions, the largest layout in this family. Right-click to check all stored fluids and their actual quantities.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended fluid output hatch has 32 bulk storage positions for large, varied product buffers. It remains an output hatch; fluids stored here are not supplied as recipe inputs.

The four tiers provide 8, 16, 24, or 32 fluid positions with large-quantity storage. Check actual amounts and fluid identities in the interface.$(br2)Configure $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO faces$(/l) to match neighboring equipment. Structure rules still decide which hatch and direction are accepted.
Extended Energy Hatches
Reinforced In

The Reinforced extended energy input hatch buffers energy for power-consuming recipes. Connect a working source and use the interface to check stored energy and capacity. It does not generate energy itself.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended energy output hatch receives energy from generating recipes. Connect a compatible consumer to draw it out. Filling the buffer can prevent further energy output.
Ultimate Input

The Ultimate extended energy input hatch offers a larger buffer and transfer limit than Reinforced. It suits high-energy recipes, but usable supply still depends on the source, connection, and structure rules.
Ultimate Output

The Ultimate extended energy output hatch offers the larger output buffer and transfer limit. It can absorb large energy products, provided there is enough room. External consumers may accept energy more slowly.

This family has Reinforced and Ultimate tiers in both directions. Capacity is the buffer size, not a promise of actual transfer speed.$(br2)Check $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l), neighboring energy capabilities, and the source or consumer. An output hatch does not replace the input needed by a consuming recipe.
Extended Combined Ports
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended combined input port supplies items and fluids from one block. It has 6 item positions and 2 fluid positions, each with bulk storage. It does not supply energy.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended combined output port receives both product types. Its 6 item positions and 2 fluid positions are separate stores. Keep compatible room available on both sides.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended combined input port has 12 item positions and 4 fluid positions. Use it for recipes needing more resource types where the structure accepts combined input.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended combined output port has 12 item positions and 4 fluid positions. Item and fluid products use independent stores; blockage of either resource can still affect the recipe.
Ultimate Input

The Ultimate extended combined input port has 18 item positions and 6 fluid positions, the largest combined layout. Check both ingredient stores before starting; capacity cannot replace missing materials.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended combined output port has 18 item positions and 6 fluid positions. It buffers many product types in one block. Arrange compatible item and fluid receivers to remove them.

All three tiers use bulk item and fluid storage. Right-click to inspect both resource groups, then configure their master and face switches separately on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto-IO page$(/l).$(br2)These ports provide neither energy nor chemicals. Whether they replace separate buses and hatches depends on the machine's structure rules.
